  "situation": "In early September 1785, the Secretary of Foreign Affairs had private intelligence that made surrender of the posts seem less certain. Congress had ordered troops raised, and reports linked that action to British attention and two regiments ordered toward Quebec. The Loyalists at the posts were estimated at six to seven thousand and reported to receive government arms and rations. Other frontier reports described Canadian encouragement for settlers near the posts and movement of people from the United States toward those lands. The credibility of the intelligence could not be ascertained, though it was consistent with other reports. The Secretary had to decide whether to bring the reports before Congress and what to recommend about their circulation.",
